subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: deployment-mode qualification and pricing ask

Hey Aditya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet you. Quick recap of where we landed and a request for pricing comparisons so we can justify internally:

- Use case: real-time clinical summarization (inference only). Not training.
- Volume (estimate): ~200M tokens/month; peak ~120 req/s; avg payload small (short prompts + 1-2k token outputs).
- Latency SLO: p95 ~200ms (lower is better).
- Security/regulatory: US-only data residency. PHI is unlikely for initial phase but data contains sensitive PII — will need SOC 2 evidence and KMS.

Could you send a short pricing comparison across: Hosted API (per-token), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity commits) and Private (VPC / on-prem licensing + infra)? Specifically we want: ballpark monthly cost, break-even point vs Hosted (tokens/month), and what commit sizes you recommend for Dedicated.

Also cc'd procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) who will handle next steps there. Happy to share a more detailed token/time distribution if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Smith
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment-mode qualification and pricing ask

Jordan — great to meet you too. Appreciate the clear requirements. High-level recap + next steps below, and I attached a short pricing overview PDF.

Recap / immediate recommendation:
- Hosted API: easiest to start, per-token billing, no infra footprint. Good for early experiments and variable traffic. For ~200M tokens/mo we'd expect a hosted cost range roughly in the mid 5-figures to low 6-figures / month depending on model family and rate limits.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended if you need predictable latency and unit-cost savings at scale. We offer monthly reserved pools (commits) and burst options. Break-even vs Hosted typically around 80M–150M tokens/month depending on model and commit size — we'll model exact numbers once we get your token mix and target model.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for customers who need full network isolation, on-prem installs, or specific compliance controls. This is an enterprise engagement (platform license + infra). Upfront setup + monthly platform fee; can be cost-efficient at very large scale (>500M tokens/mo) when you control infra.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Overview.pdf (summary tiers + sample commit sizes).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa (cc) will follow up with committed-tier examples and a short break-even table.
2) Neha (cc, solutions eng) will put together a simple cost model (spreadsheet) showing Hosted vs Dedicated for three scenarios: 100M, 200M, 500M tokens/mo.
3) Security checklist: we can provide SOC 2 report and KMS integration docs; let's schedule a short call with your security team if helpful.

If you can share a token distribution (prompt vs response avg lengths, % of peak traffic), Neha will finalize the model.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-17T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment-mode qualification and pricing ask

Jordan — looping in a couple practical numbers you can cite internally while Neha builds the detailed sheet.

Reserved commit examples (monthly):
- Small Tier: 1 x A100-equivalent GPU pool (shared across models) — good for bursty but predictable traffic. Typical effective throughput ~40–60M tokens/mo.
- Medium Tier: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs — good for steady 100–250M tokens/mo.
- Large Tier: 8+ GPUs — cost-efficient for >250M tokens/mo.

Pricing signals (very rough):
- Hosted: per-token (example): $0.00065 per token equivalent model pricing — convenient for <100M tokens/mo but can become costly as volume grows.
- Dedicated: monthly commit + per-GPU baseline; you get ~25–40% unit-cost savings vs hosted at the same model family once you hit the medium tier.
- Private: will require a platform license (~fixed monthly) + infra, typically done as a 12/24 month contract.

I'll attach a sample break-even graphic in our internal model; for now, if you expect 200M tokens/mo with steady usage, Dedicated Medium Tier is usually the sensible operational starting point and we can size commit to cover base traffic + burst headroom.

Action: Jordan, can you confirm whether 200M tokens/mo is steady-month or a peak month? Also any hard latency p95 target (you mentioned 200ms)? That will affect GPU sizing.

— Marissa
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-18T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment-mode qualification and pricing ask

Thanks all — quick clarifications:
- 200M tokens/mo is our expected steady-state after launch (month 3+). First 2 months could be ~40–60% of that.
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms if possible.
- Data residency: US only; SOC 2 required. KMS preferred.
- Procurement: please include a formal quote and SOW when you can. procurement@acmehealth.com is on copy.

If it helps, I can share a small sample of token distributions (prompt vs response averages). We'd prefer a short (1–2 page) comparison that our procurement/legal team can review.

Jordan
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: ACME cost modeling (Hosted vs Dedicated) — draft

Jordan — drafting the requested cost model and attaching the spreadsheet (ACME_cost_modeling_v1.xlsx). Quick summary below; full formulas in the sheet / link to Drive.

Summary assumptions (draft):
- Model family: r-infer-large (latency-optimized).
- Hosted per-token baseline: $0.00065 per token (blended prompt + response).
- Dedicated commit pricing: example medium tier (4 GPUs): monthly platform + GPU baseline = ~$75k/month (includes burst pool + reserved throughput). Effective unit cost at 200M tokens/mo = ~$0.00035/token (approx 46% lower than Hosted baseline in this scenario).
- Private (VPC on-prem): one-time setup + monthly license + infra. At 200M tokens/mo, amortized infra + license puts unit cost in similar range to Dedicated once you own infra, but requires upfront capex.

Break-even: Using these assumptions, Dedicated Medium tier breaks even vs Hosted at ~90–120M tokens/month depending on burst profile.

Attachments / links:
- ACME_cost_modeling_v1.xlsx (attached)
- Drive link: https://drive.google.com/acme-health-cost-model

Next steps:
1) Jordan — please confirm token distribution (avg prompt tokens / avg response tokens) and expected peak multiplier (e.g., 2x baseline).
2) I'll update the sheet and produce a 1–2 page procurement-ready comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) including SLO/latency notes and contract options (monthly commit sizes, minimum terms).
3) We can set a 30-minute pricing review with procurement and security to walk the numbers and get a formal quote.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: ACME_cost_modeling_v1.xlsx)
